question: The radii of the two concentric circles are 27 cm and 18 cm. The area (in cm²) of the closed figure bounded by the boundaries of the circle is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Area of a circular ring = π × (R − r) × (R + r)

Substitute R = 27 and r = 18 into the formula:

⇒ Area = π × (27 − 18) × (27 + 18)

⇒ Area = π × 9 × 45

⇒ Area = 405π

**∴ The correct answer is 405π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Outer radius of the circle (R) = 27 cm

⇒ Inner radius of the circle (r) = 18 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of the bounded region (Ring) = Area of outer circle − Area of inner circle

⇒ Area = πR² − πr² = π(R² − r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c73cfae67109021ad082c3e0fe1844f1b58261101cc8bbd354f6f05c1b8cd46.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = π × (27)² − π × (18)²

⇒ Area = π × (729 − 324)

⇒ Area = 405π

**∴ The correct answer is 405π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concentric Circles

Concentric circles are circles that share the exact same center point but have different radii. The region enclosed between two concentric circles is often referred to as an annulus or a circular ring.

Width of the Circular Ring

The thickness or width of the ring is uniformly distributed and can be calculated by subtracting the inner radius from the outer radius: Width = R − r.

Algebraic Identities

When solving questions involving the difference of squares, applying the algebraic identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) will severely reduce the calculation time and prevent squaring large values.
